intro: The Enclave at Commanders Point is a gated group of attached homes near Commander's Point Marina on Lake Travis. CleanzATX cleans windows here, and a group of neighbors in one community makes scheduling easy, with Tyler quoting every home himself.

sections.h2: What Enclave at Commanders Point homes are like
paragraphs: These are townhome style homes, attached to each other, in a small gated community near the marina. A typical home is about 2,400 sq ft and sells for around $550K. The Enclave at Commanders Point association handles shared areas. It sits close to the marina and the RR 620 corridor, so shopping and the lake are both minutes away.

Attached homes mean shared walls and limited yard space. That changes how we plan a visit. We have to stay on your side of the property line, keep an eye on neighboring patios, and make sure no one else is affected by our water. If you live in the middle of a row, only the front and back have exterior glass. End units have side windows too, so the count differs from one unit to the next.

sections.h2: What Enclave at Commanders Point windows deal with
paragraphs: Being near a marina means lake air and mist reach the glass. Hard water from the lake leaves white mineral spots, which can build up faster on windows that are not cleaned regularly. Windows near parking areas and driveways also pick up dust and road grime. Dust and pollen settle on balcony glass and sliding doors quickly, since attached homes have fewer walls to shelter them.

Attached homes often have fewer exterior walls but more upper windows, balconies or patio doors. Screens and sliding door tracks collect pollen and webs. We clean screens at $5 each and tracks at $5, and we treat spots at $10 per pane. The lake carries minerals, and those are the spots you see after a windy day.

sections.h2: How we work Enclave at Commanders Point
paragraphs: Gate access is the first step. Give us the code or the contact name, and let your association know if it expects vendor notice. Our pure water system runs from the truck, and water fed poles reach upper windows from the ground, so we do not need ladders on shared walls or balconies. If several neighbors want service, we can schedule them together, which keeps the visits short.

A 2,400 sq ft home comes to about $240 for exterior windows at $0.10 per sq ft. Expect roughly two to two and a half hours on site for the outside. Add inside cleaning at $15 per window total for both sides, and allow another hour.

faq.q: Do you need to enter my home?
faq.a: For exterior glass, no. We clean from the ground with water fed poles. For inside windows, someone needs to be home or arrange access, and we cover floors with drop cloths. Text us a day that works and we will confirm the time.

Send the code or a contact when you text. We handle the rest and keep equipment on your side of the property. Your association may have its own vendor rules, so check with your manager if you are unsure.

faq.q: Can we book more than one townhome at the same time?
faq.a: Yes. Neighbors who book together help us keep travel short. Text the group details and we can build a visit around it. You do not have to coordinate with a neighbor, but you can if you prefer.

faq.q: What does it cost for a 2,400 sq ft townhome?
faq.a: Exterior windows are about $240 at $0.10 per sq ft, or $10 per window. Both sides of each window cost $15. The minimum job is $200. That works out to roughly 24 windows, based on about 10 per 1,000 sq ft.

faq.q: Do you clean patios and balconies?
faq.a: Yes. Patios and pool decks are cleaned by hand, so water does not run over a neighbor. Flatwork is $0.18 per sq ft for concrete, with a $250 minimum. Hand cleaning keeps water off neighboring patios and shared walkways.
